rows.name: Dependency graph of actions
rows.offer: Describes builds, deploys, runs and tests as one graph of actions with dependencies, so the right things start in the right order.

rows.name: Print the dependency graph
rows.offer: A command prints the dependency relationships across the whole project so you can see what depends on what.

flisk.reason: Flisk already knows every resource's dependsOn from service.json, so printing it as text or JSON for people and agents fits a local tool.

rows.acceptance: A `flisk` command (or `flisk stack` subcommand) and an MCP tool listed in cli/src/mcp/tools.ts print the dependsOn graph as JSON; evidence becomes a command item plus an mcpTool item.

ice.basis: Impact 5: helps people and agents understand start order but does not unblock anyone; confidence 7: Garden documents the command and dependsOn data is already in the registry; ease 6: data exists in runtime/discovery, only a CLI/MCP view is new.

rows.name: Preview before running
rows.offer: A plan command shows which actions would run without changing anything, so you can review before deploying.

rows.name: Validate configuration
rows.offer: A validate command checks the project config files for errors and exits non-zero when something is wrong.

rows.name: Status of project and actions
rows.offer: Prints the full status of the environment and every action as structured output.

rows.name: Live log streaming
rows.offer: Shows logs of one or more deployed services and can follow new lines as they arrive.

flisk.reason: `flisk logs` prints a bounded snapshot of recent logs; live following happens in `flisk ui` and Tilt, not as a scriptable stream.

rows.name: Interactive dev console
rows.offer: Starts the stack with an interactive console and streaming logs in one command.

rows.name: Shell into a running service
rows.offer: Runs a command or opens an interactive shell inside the container of a deployed service.

flisk.reason: Developers and coding agents often need to run a one-off command inside a running service, and Flisk only has logs and restart today.

rows.acceptance: A `flisk exec <resource> -- <cmd>` command (docker exec in container mode, a child process in the resource's directory in native mode) plus an MCP tool in cli/src/mcp/tools.ts; evidence becomes a command item and an mcpTool item.

ice.basis: Impact 6: removes a common docker-exec detour for people and gives agents a safe way to run a command; confidence 7: documented Garden command and a known gap versus Compose; ease 5: Docker case is a thin wrapper around cli/src/commands/logs.ts-style container lookup but native mode needs its own path.

rows.name: Live code sync into services
rows.offer: Syncs local source changes into a running container with several sync modes so you do not rebuild the image.

rows.name: Local process actions
rows.offer: Runs builds and long-lived dev servers directly on the host next to containerised services, for hybrid setups.

rows.name: Migrate from Docker Compose
rows.offer: A guide converts a docker-compose project into Garden config by hand.

rows.name: Tests as first-class actions
rows.offer: Tests are a built-in action kind you define in config and run from the CLI against the environment.

flisk.reason: Flisk scaffolds vitest and playwright test setups per resource but has no `flisk test` command that runs them against the running stack.

rows.name: Skip unchanged builds and tests
rows.offer: Hashes each action's sources, config and upstream actions so only changed pieces rebuild or re-test.

flisk.reason: Flisk relies on layered Docker images and Tilt change detection for rebuilds; there is no content-hash that lets a re-run of resources or tests be skipped explicitly.

rows.name: Scripted command sequences
rows.offer: Defines named sequences of CLI commands and shell steps in config that run the same way locally and in CI.

flisk.reason: A committed, named sequence such as up then migrate then smoke test fits a local runner and is what people otherwise keep in Makefiles.

rows.acceptance: service.json or the project config accepts a `workflows` block and `flisk workflow <name>` runs its steps; evidence becomes a command item for `flisk workflow` and a text item in docs/service-json.md.

ice.basis: Impact 4: Makefiles and shell scripts already cover this for most users; confidence 5: Garden's users value it but Flisk users have not asked; ease 3: needs a new config schema in discovery plus a new command and error handling.

rows.name: Project-defined custom commands
rows.offer: Lets a team add its own named commands, with steps and arguments, that show up in the tool's help.

flisk.reason: Named shortcuts for a team's usual start-up flow (which stack, which flags) would shorten onboarding without leaving the CLI.

rows.acceptance: A project-level manifest key defines commands that `flisk help` lists and `flisk <name>` runs; evidence becomes a command item for the sample command and a text item in docs/service-json.md.

ice.basis: Impact 3: stacks already group resources and shell aliases cover the rest; confidence 5: only Garden documentation as evidence; ease 4: cli/src/commands/stack.ts and help.ts give a place but dynamic commands need careful naming rules.

rows.name: Reusable config templates
rows.offer: Teams write templates that render several actions from a few inputs, hiding boilerplate from app developers.

flisk.reason: Flisk generates services from built-in templates (`flisk resource`, `flisk project agent-stack`) but a team cannot register its own template.

rows.name: Variables and template strings
rows.offer: Config values can use ${...} template strings that reference variables, other actions and the environment.

flisk.reason: Flisk has plain params and secrets per resource in service.json but no expression language to reference other resources' values.

rows.name: Import actions from other repos
rows.offer: Pulls actions or whole config from other git repositories pinned to a branch, tag or commit.

flisk.reason: Flisk discovers services across several local scan roots but does not clone or pin remote repositories.

rows.name: Same config in CI
rows.offer: The configuration used on a laptop also runs unchanged in CI pipelines.

flisk.reason: Flisk documents a GitHub Actions job that verifies files and boots a stack, but treats CI as a throwaway environment, not a delivery path.

rows.name: Export CLI traces to APM
rows.offer: Runs a local OpenTelemetry collector during a command and exports timing data to Datadog, New Relic, Honeycomb or OTLP.

flisk.reason: Flisk ships an optional monitoring feature (SigNoz) for the apps it runs, but does not trace its own CLI commands.

rows.name: Team-shared build and test cache
rows.offer: Stores action versions in a hosted backend so teammates and CI skip work someone already did.

flisk.reason: It depends on a hosted service and shared state across people; Flisk is a local runtime with no account or backend.

rows.name: Hosted remote image builder
rows.offer: Builds container images on managed remote compute with shared layer caches.

flisk.reason: Remote build compute is a paid cloud service; Flisk builds on the developer's own machine by design.

rows.name: Per-PR preview environments
rows.offer: Creates an isolated environment per pull request or developer in a shared remote cluster.

flisk.reason: These live in a remote Kubernetes cluster; Flisk is local only and leaves staging and previews to cluster tooling.

rows.name: Automatic environment cleanup
rows.offer: A cluster agent pauses or deletes idle environments after a configured time.

flisk.reason: It needs an agent running inside a Kubernetes cluster; local stacks stop with `flisk down`.

rows.name: Local Kubernetes provider
rows.offer: Targets Docker Desktop, minikube or similar local clusters and picks the context automatically.

flisk.reason: Flisk runs services on Docker or as plain processes and does not need or emit Kubernetes resources.

rows.name: Kubernetes, Helm and IaC deploys
rows.offer: Deploys Kubernetes manifests and Helm charts and applies Terraform or Pulumi stacks as part of the graph.

flisk.reason: Flisk does not deploy or replace Helm and IaC tools; production policy stays with those tools (docs/with-helm.md).

rows.name: Hosted secrets and variables
rows.offer: Stores variables and encrypted secrets in a cloud service, scoped to environments and users, and imports them into config.

flisk.reason: A hosted multi-user secret store needs an account service; Flisk keeps secret values in the project .env and only names them in service.json.

rows.name: Mount host folders into pods
rows.offer: An experimental alternative to file sync that mounts host directories into Kubernetes pods through hostPath.

flisk.reason: It only exists for Kubernetes pods; Flisk already bind-mounts or live-updates containers through Docker and Tilt.

rows.name: Hosted dashboard and history
rows.offer: A web dashboard shows environment URLs, logs and command history for the team.

flisk.reason: It is a hosted team product; Flisk shows the local stack in `flisk ui` and the Tilt UI.
